technology_name: Sustainable Construction Materials from Industrial Waste (CLSM)
institution: KSCSTE - National Transportation Planning and Research Centre (NATPAC)
problem_solved: Disposing of massive quantities of construction debris (concrete/quarry waste) while addressing the difficulty of backfilling tight utility trenches where mechanical soil compaction is impossible.
description: Controlled Low-Strength Materials (CLSM) are self-compacting, highly flowable cementitious slurries engineered to replace compacted soil backfills. This specific innovation optimizes a low-cement mix using industrial byproducts: 30% fly ash, 50% quarry waste, and 20% concrete waste with just 3% cement. The formulation maintains a high flowability of 250 mm and is physically engineered to stay below a strict 28-day compressive strength ceiling (0.7 MPa) to ensure it can be easily dug out later using standard hand tools.
applications:
• Self-leveling backfills for underground utility, pipe, and cable trenches

• Structural fill for abandoned underground storage tanks, mines, and basements

• Eco-friendly sub-base layers for municipal road construction and sidewalks

• Commercial formulation manufacturing for green ready-mix concrete suppliers
